citation: Alexander AS, Nitz DA (2017). Spatially periodic activation patterns of retrosplenial cortex encode route sub-spaces and distance travelled. bioRxiv 100537 v1 (published as Curr Biol 27:1551-1560)
environment_type: closed plus-shaped track with recurrent segments
environment_size: Closed plus-shaped track with recurrent structure at several scales, 12 segments; 1 cm edges, open view of the room; route rewarded at one point. Track lengths are not given in the text read (dimensions are in Fig. 1B)
measure: Correlation of population rate vectors between odd and even trials (position x position matrix), used for position reconstruction
normalization: Rate profiles max-normalized in figures; normalization for the reconstruction not stated
simultaneous_or_pooled: not stated; populations resampled from 5 to 140 neurons out of 229, so pooled across rats and sessions is likely
far_behaviour: Off-diagonal peaks repeat at analogous positions on same-shape segments, spaced at quarter-route scale; CA1 matrices lack these repeats
quote_or_reading: "Unlike matrices for the CA1 ensemble, off-diagonal correlations for RSC ensembles exhibited repeating patterns across the track." "significant correlation peaks were observed for analogous route positions with spacing at the scale of route quarter sections." Reconstruction error RSC "1.9 ± 2.7 centimeters", CA1 "5.2 ± 6.7 centimeters" (141 CA1 place cells, 3 rats)
status: preprint; text via WebFetch excerpts; curve not read
verified_in: this sweep (source: bioRxiv 100537v1 full-text HTML read through WebFetch excerpts, quoted sentences only; curl to bioRxiv was rate-limited; figures not seen)
notes: Within one environment and session (odd vs even trials), so it counts as a cross-half kernel, but no width or zero crossing is reported and the figure was not seen. The kernel is not monotonic: it aliases at repeated segment shapes. The Fig. 6 'distance reconstruction' correlates first-half and mirrored second-half vectors around a symmetry point (error 2.09 cm), which measures distance from the symmetry point, not a kernel.
